reden: Not detected. The report’s closest item is the refund-based reentrancy in _handleTrade that bypasses the 10‑minute share lock and enables reward-grab during the buy refund callback. It does not describe reentering createCred/_createCredInternal to overwrite creds[credIdCounter] before incrementation, nor the curve-switching angle (cheap curve on first create, overwrite to expensive curve via reentrancy) that enables draining. The code path and fix differ: the described vuln hinges on reentrancy into createCred and overwriting state prior to credIdCounter++, whereas the report focuses on timestamp update ordering and lack of nonReentrant on the single-trade path for lock enforcement. Fixing the report’s issue (e.g., writing the timestamp before refund) wouldn’t fix the createCred overwrite attack; conversely, adding nonReentrant to createCred (the described fix) wouldn’t by itself address the lock-bypass finding. Therefore they are different vulnerabilities.
